title: Specy system requirements
description: A .sysreq file as a document: what `specy convert --to json|yaml` emits for a requirements file, and what `specy convert` reads back into a .sysreq. One entry per `requirements "…" scoped-to Context { }` block, in file order; inside a set, the loose requirements and the modules keep their order. A requirement is an EARS statement with its pattern, MoSCoW priority, provenance (`source`, a PRD id or name) and traceability (dependencies, conflicts, decomposition, the domain elements that satisfy it).

parser.description: Which parser wrote the document; consumers pin the minimum version whose shape they understand.

requirementId.description: REQ-<CONTEXT>[-<SEGMENT>]-<NNN>, stable for the life of the requirement.

scope.description: The bounded context or organization the set is scoped to (`scoped-to`), a PascalCase name.

prdSources.description: Paths of the .prd files the requirements trace to, as written.

requirements.description: Requirements declared directly in the set.

pattern.description: The EARS pattern of the statement.

rationale.description: The `::` justification: why the requirement exists. Does not change its meaning.

source.description: The PRD element this requirement formalizes: its stable id (FEAT-001, US-004, AC-004-02) or its name ("Job: …", "Constraint: …").

dependsOn.description: Requirements that must be satisfied before this one can be.

conflictsWith.description: Requirements in tension with this one: both cannot be fully satisfied at once.

decomposedInto.description: Context-level requirements an organization-level one derives.

satisfiedBy.description: The domain elements that satisfy the requirement, by role.

satisfactionLink.description: One `satisfied-by` entry. `target` is the domain element as the DSL names it: `Type`, `Type.field`, or `Type."operation label"`; absent for `satisfied-by-infrastructure`, which names no element.
